Nerve root syndromes Classic nerve root syndrome is characterized by radicular pain arising from nerve root impingement due to herniated discs. A similar syndrome can also be produced by inflammation and irritation, which may explain why patients whose presentation is consistent with this diagnosis respond to conservative therapies. Impingement pain tends to be sharp, well localized, and can be associated with paresthesia, whereas irritation pain tends to be dull, poorly localized, and without paresthesia. diseases.name: Cervical Strain
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire addresses key features of cervical strain, such as a history of trauma or sudden movement, and localized neck pain. RAG source rag-93469eb32013b428 mentions that the primary diagnostic challenge is differentiating cervical strain from other causes of neck pain, particularly after trauma, which aligns with questions about triggering events like injury or accidents.

diseases.name: Cervical Radiculopathy
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire specifically asks about symptoms radiating to the arms or hands, including numbness, tingling, and weakness. This aligns with the description of radicular pain from nerve root impingement, which can be sharp and associated with paresthesia, as described in the context of nerve root syndromes.

diseases.name: Retropharyngeal Abscess
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire includes questions about fever, difficulty swallowing (dysphagia), and neck stiffness. These are key symptoms of a retropharyngeal abscess, a serious infection in the deep spaces of the neck.

diseases.name: Spinal Cord Neoplasm
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire explores the nature of the pain and the presence of neurological deficits. Pain is noted as the most common early complaint in adult patients with spinal cord neoplasms, often followed by progressive spinal cord dysfunction, which could manifest as the arm/hand symptoms queried.

diseases.name: Lyme Disease
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire asks about systemic symptoms like fever, chills, and neck stiffness. These are characteristic symptoms of early disseminated (Stage 2) Lyme disease, which can also present with myalgias and arthralgias that could be perceived as neck pain.

diseases.name: Neck Trauma
diseases.rationale: Several questions focus on a history of injury or accident, as well as symptoms like difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) or breathing (dyspnea). These are important signs to evaluate in the context of potential neck trauma, which can involve injury to the esophagus, pharynx, or spinal cord.
